description:
Design the canonical ownership cutover from the flat, core-owned tuning schema to one versioned profile envelope with crate-owned typed sections.

## Background

The standing designs `dev/active/220cab0b/design.md` and `dev/active/7d824b2f/design.md` put `permanent.gray_chunk_subsets` in `gf2-core::tuning` under D4 and owner decision DEC-B11. That preserves the dependency edge `gf2-algebra -> gf2-core`, but it makes the lower-level crate define, validate, serialize, and document vocabulary for a permanent algorithm owned by `gf2-algebra`. The epic owner supersedes that durable ownership shape: tuning semantics belong to the crate that owns the algorithm and selection boundary, while shared profile mechanics remain one inward dependency.

The reviewed direction is profile format 2: `gf2-core` owns a generic envelope, explicit typed-section registry, deterministic encoding, provenance types, and the single process-wide install/resolve cell. `gf2-core` and `gf2-algebra` each own their typed selector section, defaults, validation, codec, calibration behavior, and strict owner-only envelope. Every load validates all present sections through registered owner codecs; a registered section that is absent resolves to its owner's conservative default. A repository composer that links both crates assembles and validates the complete envelope from the authoritative owner artifacts. There is no partial-composite load, opaque skipped section, or second wire representation. Independent architecture and caller-inventory review confirmed that this strict owner-envelope flow serves every current and planned epic consumer while removing speculative subset state.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed design fixes the profile-format-2 wire shape and Rust API for the generic envelope, stable section IDs, erased codecs without unsafe code, explicit registry construction, deterministic encoding, one atomic install/resolve authority, and crate-owned typed active-section access. It defines one strict load convention: every present section requires its registered owner codec and complete validation; any unknown or unregistered present section is rejected; an absent section may resolve to its owning type's conservative default. Crate-owned owner-only envelopes and the mechanically assembled complete envelope use this same wire form, and no partial/skipped-section mechanism exists.
- [hard] REQ-02: The design fixes failure and test semantics: late install is a hard error carrying the first-resolution call site; calibration producers exit nonzero on it; per-section resolution reports `Installed`, `DefaultedMissing`, or `FrozenBeforeInstall`; install-order tests run through one named fresh-subprocess helper rather than a resettable alternate global.
- [hard] REQ-03: The design assigns every semantic responsibility to its owner. `gf2-core` owns common mechanism and only core selector vocabulary; `gf2-algebra` owns `PermanentSelectors`, `CHUNK_SUBSETS`, its admissible range, codec, active accessor, baked values, and calibration component. It preserves the inward production dependency and identifies every current symbol, test, artifact, and prose site removed or amended at cutover.
- [hard] REQ-04: The design fixes versioning and evidence composition: envelope assembly provenance and digest coexist with per-section measurement provenance; every codec rejects unsupported section schema versions before decoding selectors; serde/codecs stay behind non-default tuning-profile features; authoritative crate-owned envelopes compose into a repository-level complete envelope under one outer benchmark lock with no build side effect, and validation proves each composed section is canonically identical to its owner artifact.
- [hard] REQ-05: The design provides a canonical-cutover migration for the active flat profile and baked evidence anchor without relabeling measurements or weakening provenance. It defines the clean intermediate artifact, archive treatment if historical bytes remain necessary, storage paths, final stale-symbol/prose sweep, and dependencies/amendments for `389aa4de`, `eaae1b56`, `a83583e0`, and `dbd8787d`. The final tree has no core permanent tuning symbol, active flat profile, flat reader, compatibility alias, dual ownership, partial-composite loader, or skipped-section state.

## Notes

- Append supersession amendments to closed designs and decisions rather than rewriting their historical record.
- Baked selector constants remain crate-owned at their selection sites; they are not dynamically read from the envelope.
- A neutral production tuning crate is out of scope because `gf2-core` has no production dependency on another gf2 workspace crate.
title: Design crate-owned typed tuning sections
